corpus_intended_use: Preregistered public development corpus for the Codex-only three-arm comparison. It asks again whether the full reviewer workflow beats the pattern catalog alone, on cases written after the severity-exception wording was added to the skill, and whether documented severity exceptions are applied on cases no model has seen. It is not sealed and does not establish generalization.
corpus_contamination_risk: The corpus is inspectable and was written by the same author who wrote the reviewer references it exercises. It was designed from the reference contracts alone, without reading any v9 run report. Every result must disclose that exposure and remain development evidence.

scoring.source_rendering_contract: Each embedded source line is prefixed with its 1-based number, right-aligned to six columns, and a tab, as `nl -ba` prints it. The prefix is display-only; findings must cite that number as `line`.
scoring.label_semantics_contract: Findings still match exact (pattern_id, severity, file, line) tuples. A finding label matches when a report hits its primary tuple or any accepted_alternatives tuple, and counts as one true positive however many of those tuples are reported. An optional label is excluded from true-positive and false-negative denominators; a report matching it is not a false positive and is counted separately as an optional match. fp_guard labels keep their meaning.
scoring.stability_contract: A finding or optional label is stable when the number of successful repetitions that matched any of its tuples meets the strict-majority rule. A stable prediction is a false positive only when it matches no finding or optional label tuple.

schedule.freeze_policy: Freeze sources, labels, and protocol before the first measured run. Any later edit creates a new version.
schedule.design_disclosure: Designed after reviewer holdout v9 ran and the reviewer skill then changed: the SKILL.md Quick Reference now calls each listed severity the usual case and names documented exceptions, and pattern-reference.md #1 states a P0/P1 severity rule. Those changes were written after v9 was seen, so v9 cannot test them. V10 asks the same question on 30 new synthetic cases (15 Playwright, 15 Cypress) that no model has run: does the full workflow beat the catalog alone, and does severity-exception handling generalize to unseen cases? Eleven cases hinge on a documented severity exception or boundary (#1, #2, #4 sub-IDs, #4k, #5a/#5b, #8b, #12, #3/#15, #18, #23), with a guard at the other severity on the same line wherever the contract forces one and an optional label where it supports two readings. Ten are decided by rules that live only in the full workflow references: semantic-review.md sweeps and anchors, review-scope.md framework-scope and project-convention rules, the reporting.md P0 boundary, and scanner-workflow.md JUSTIFIED handling. The rest are ordinary true positives and four clean cases. The cases were designed from the reference contracts alone, without reading any v9 run report or per-case v9 result. Labels were written by one author, then checked by two blind model labelers (Claude and Codex) and a model arbiter before any measured run. It keeps the v9 host, arms, thresholds, seed, strict-majority stability rule, numbered sources, scoring contract, and five repetitions. The corpus is public development evidence that was inspected while designing this protocol; it is not sealed and does not establish generalization. Before any run, the single host was moved from Codex gpt-5.6-sol to Claude claude-opus-5 because the Codex subscription quota was nearly exhausted and the Fable model was usage-limited. Claude runs with every tool disabled and no permission mode (claude_permission_mode off), so the plan-file failure that ended the v5 and v6 Claude runs cannot occur. Results are not comparable across hosts with v8 or v9; the full versus catalog-only question is answered within this one host.

execution_identity.run_identity_capture: Capture the resolved runner path and CLI version in each report. Do not pin user-specific absolute paths or binary digests in this public protocol.
execution_identity.attestation_limit: Reported execution identity is provenance, not cryptographic attestation.

prompt_arms.matrix_requirement: Run a separate complete host matrix for full, catalog-only, and no-skill.

arm_comparison.temporal_validity_limit: Reported start/completion timestamps, fixed order, non-overlap, and a 12-hour first-start-to-last-completion window reduce arm-position and time-drift confounding but do not cryptographically attest time or identify or freeze provider backend revisions.

uncertainty.interpretation_limit: Bootstrap intervals describe case-resampling sensitivity on this fixed public case set. They do not quantify model-run stochasticity and are not population confidence intervals, independent replications, or release-grade causal inference.

decision.failure_semantics: Every threshold must pass against each control. A complete matrix that misses any threshold is FAIL, not partial evidence.

claim_policy.pass: Development skill-lift evidence is limited to this fixed public corpus, declared model identifiers, captured CLI versions, prompts, and schedule; provider backend snapshots are not attested.
claim_policy.partial_results: Descriptive arm metrics may be published, but never as a causal or partial skill-lift claim.

decision.point_estimate_limits: Threshold crossings on this small fixed public development corpus are descriptive signals. The corpus is public and inspectable. Confidence intervals accompany point estimates; sealing, independent blind evaluation after publication, cryptographic runner attestation, cross-provider replication, and population-level generalization are not established.

cross_host_decision.aggregation_intent: Single-host Claude protocol; the single declared host is evaluated directly and no cross-provider claim is allowed.

evidence_limitations.message: prompt-complete zero-tool execution stages parent authentication material, not a disposable scoped credential; this report is development evidence and is not release-eligible
the no-skill arm receives no detection rules or workflow; a minimal ID, title, and severity legend is shared only for fair exact-match output scoring
